exploration.title: Machine Workshop
exploration.subject: Engineering
exploration.summary: Change a lever, pulley system or geared hoist and compare the effort with the distance moved.
exploration.question: When a machine reduces the force you need, what changes about how far you must move?
exploration.explanation: A lever turns around a pivot; supporting rope sections share a pulley load; gears transfer turning motion. Mechanical advantage compares the load force with the input force. In an ideal machine, reducing the input force requires more input travel for the same lift. The geared hoist has an equal-radius crank handle and lifting drum, so its force and distance readings describe the hand and load. This model assumes slow lifting with no friction, rope stretch or machine weight.

experiments.title: Rope sections
experiments.instruction: Choose Rope sections. With two supporting rope sections instead of one, what happens to the pulling force? Select your prediction, then Set baseline and Use two sections. Keep the load at 40 kg and lift it 0.5 m. Compare one supporting section with two. Count the sections lifting the moving load, not the wheels.
experiments.observe: Pulling force falls from 392.4 N to 196.2 N; rope pulled increases from 0.5 m to 1.0 m. Input and output work are both 196.2 J. Why must you pull farther when less force lifts the same load through the same height? Use force × distance as evidence.

experiments.title: Gear turns
experiments.instruction: Choose Gear turns. What happens to the number of crank turns when a 12-tooth driver turns a 48-tooth gear instead of a 12-tooth gear? Select your prediction, then Set baseline and Use 48 driven teeth. Keep the load at 40 kg and lift at 0.5 m. Both the crank and rope drum have a 0.2 m radius. Change only the driven gear tooth count.
experiments.observe: Crank turns increase from 0.40 to 1.59; input torque falls from 78.48 to 19.62 N·m. Output torque stays at 78.48 N·m, and work stays at 196.2 J. Torque is a turning effect. Why does a larger driven gear turn less per input turn while providing greater output torque than input torque?

exploration.misconception: A machine can reduce the force needed without reducing the ideal work needed. Force and distance must be considered together.
